items.title: [FDD Diary #1] I Thought It Worked
content:
Can't code. Built a product anyway.
Then the whole system died.

ChatGPT for two years. Ask a question, get a code block.
Copy. Paste. Error.
Copy the error. Ask again. Another code block.
Paste. Error.

Never escaped that loop.

Then I heard about Claude Code. Installed it.
Typed "make me a to-do app" out of habit.

But something different happened.
It didn't show me code. It made the files directly.

Folders created. Code written. Packages installed.

Wait.
I don't have to copy-paste?

"Type npm start."
I typed it.
A to-do app appeared in my browser.

Five minutes.
What took three hours with ChatGPT took five minutes.

"Now a notes app." Done.
"Connect a database." Done.
"Login feature." Done.

Everything I asked for worked.
Nothing seemed impossible.

Built a stock screener. Two days.
586 US stocks, three strategies, done in three minutes.

"Run this automatically every day." Done.
Something called a cron job. Don't know what that is but it runs every morning.

"Send results to Slack." Done.

Three days in I had five agents running.
One collects data, one organizes, one analyzes, one reports, one monitors.
Something like that.

They ran. Everything ran.

Am I a genius?
I knew I wasn't. But it felt that way.

"I can build anything with this."

That thought.
That feeling.
That was the trap.

🔗 Full post: https://vibecode.town/posts/i-thought-it-worked

items.title: [FDD Diary #2] Monday Morning
content:
The build crashed.
Couldn't read the error.
Because I'm not a developer.

I built it the same way I built the to-do app.

"Add file sync." Done.
"Add remote commands." Done.
"Add an agent for monitoring." Done.
"Add process management." Done.

Like assembling IKEA furniture.
Read the step. Screw this into that. Next step.

I never stopped to ask if the pieces fit together.
I just kept adding parts.

Monday morning.
Made coffee. Turned on the monitor.

The whole system was dead.

Friday it was fine.
Changed something Saturday. Don't remember what.
Monday — nothing works.

Opened the code. Can't read it. But I can scroll.
Scrolled. And scrolled.

10,847 lines.
Almost half was duplicated. 4,200 lines.

Five agents built the same function five different ways.
Three date formatters. Two config parsers.
Four ways to validate input.

Nobody noticed.
Not the AI. Not me.

Ran a security audit. Line 847. Shell injection.

This tool connects my computers over a network.
External connections come in. Commands get sent.
A shell injection means anyone can walk in and run anything.

That's not a bug. That's a door.
That door was open the whole time.

This wasn't IKEA furniture.
This was raw lumber.
And I'd been using an Allen key the whole time.

That night I shut everything down.
Stared at ten thousand lines.
"What the hell am I even building?"

🔗 Full post: https://vibecode.town/posts/everything-broke-monday

items.title: [FDD Diary #3] Nothing Works
content:
Forty-five minutes became twelve.
Without reading a single line of code.

Three computers at home. Two desktops, one laptop.
I want to work from my laptop outside and still use the machines at home.
Files sync automatically. Send commands remotely. See results on my laptop.

That's the wish.
But nothing on the market does this.

Tried them one by one.

KVM switch.
Works at home. Connect from outside? Nope.
Physical only. Network? Not supported.
Half-assed.

Remote Desktop.
Usable. But slow.
Move the cursor, it follows 0.3 seconds later.
Video? Slideshow.
Connection drops with every Wi-Fi hiccup.

Cloud sync.
Files sync. That's it. Can't run processes.
And my files go through someone else's server.
10GB dataset to the cloud and back? USB is faster.

Git.
Code? Perfect. Everything else? No.

This is where I ended up.
KVM + Remote Desktop + cloud + Git + terminal.
Five apps running simultaneously just to get "barely okay."

Barely.
Okay.

Can't work on "barely okay."
Every morning: open five apps, remember where everything is, manually fix sync conflicts.

That's not work. That's busywork.

So I decided to build it myself.

But here's the important part.
It wasn't "decided to build it" first.
It was "figured out why nothing works" first.

Every product I tried, I knew exactly what pissed me off about it.
KVM — no network. RDP — slow and drops. Cloud — files only, someone else's server. Git — code only.

I didn't know it yet.
But that list of grievances?
That was the beginning of a spec.

I just didn't have the word for it.

🔗 Full post: https://vibecode.town/posts/frustration-is-the-spec
